audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows disagreed with the packet and the already-settled mirror; the page gave Riven levels 2, 3, first item and two items while its own whys say Gragas owns each of them.
audit.why: The mirror set this chart to Skill / Gragas / Skill / Gragas / Gragas / Gragas / Skill in both layers, and the packet chart is identical. whys[1] ('you cannot match that trade pattern yet'), whys[5] ('fights cost you more than they cost him') and whys[6] ('genuinely even') were already describing that chart.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-6 flipped as one atomic group across both layers, Gragas rows to 4/10 and Skill rows to 5/10. Difficulty moved to 5/10 to match the mirror and a 50.19% win rate.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late spike claimed 'Gragas's AP scaling on Q pool regeneration'. Barrel Roll leaves no pool and regenerates nothing. wants.foe[2] repeated the invention as 'Pool sustain from Q (Barrel Roll)'.
audit.why: Gragas's sustain is Happy Hour, his passive, which heals him periodically on ability use — so his sustain scales with how often he casts anything, not with a Q pool. A player told to avoid a puddle will misplay a lane where the real sustain follows him everywhere.
audit.corrected: Both strings now name Happy Hour and tie his attrition to cast frequency plus Drunken Rage's damage cut.
sources: enemyKit P text 'Gragas periodically heals upon using a skill'

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing said that Valor's shield does not stop Explosive Cask's knockback, and wants.you[0] told the player to trade 'before Gragas can activate his W', which is not a window that exists.
audit.why: Drunken Rage is a 5-second cooldown costing 30 mana — it is effectively always available, so 'get in before he presses W' is unactionable. The real tell is the 1-second sip animation and the reset it puts on his next attack. And Explosive Cask displaces through the shield: Valor absorbs damage, not movement, so the counterplay is positioning (a wall behind him), not shielding.
audit.corrected: wants.you[0] rebuilt around the 5-second Drunken Rage cycle, wants.foe[0] around the sip-and-auto-reset tell, whys[4] around the shield-does-not-stop-displacement rule from the mirror.
sources: enemyKit W cd '5', cost 30, flags autoReset

audit.whatIsWrong: Body Slam is named as the tracked cooldown on every screen of this entry but its duration was never given.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14 seconds at rank 1 and only drops to 12 at rank 5 — the longest gap in his kit and the entire commit window.
audit.corrected: whys[1] and breakdown.difficulty now carry the 14-second number.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Body Slam and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Body Slam's 14s and stay disciplined.

edits.before: Gragas gets Body Slam (E) and W at Level 2: he E's into you, pops W to absorb your burst, and backs out — you cannot match that trade pattern yet.
edits.after: Body Slam arrives at 2 — he charges in, sips Drunken Rage to cut your burst, and walks out. It is a 14s cooldown, so punish only the miss.

edits.before: At Level 6 Gragas's Explosive Cask can knock you out of your Q chain mid-combo, wasting Wind Slash and turning your all-in into free damage for him.
edits.after: Explosive Cask knocks you out of your Q chain at 6 — Valor blocks the damage but not the displacement, so open the all-in with a wall behind him.

edits.before: At 2+ items Gragas's AP scaling on Q pool regeneration and W reduces to a war of attrition that Riven cannot consistently win — convert any lead into objectives rather than prolonged side-lane duels.
edits.after: At 2+ items Happy Hour heals him off every cast and Drunken Rage cuts what lands, turning the duel into attrition Riven loses — convert leads into objectives, not prolonged side-lane duels.

edits.before: Force short trades with E-shield into W stun before Gragas can activate his W damage-reduction bubble
edits.after: Trade in the second after Drunken Rage's damage cut expires — it is only a 5s cooldown, so time it.

edits.before: Activate W damage-reduction the instant you land E into you, eating your full burst window
edits.after: Drink Drunken Rage on the way in — the 1-second sip is his tell, and it cuts your whole burst

edits.before: Pool sustain from Q (Barrel Roll) across the lane phase until his bulk items come online and he outruns your damage
edits.after: Heal off Happy Hour every cast through the lane phase until his bulk items come online and he outruns your damage

notes: Both of the packet's suspectNames here are FALSE POSITIVES: Explosive Cask and Body Slam are the correct Riot names (the packet flagged the plural 'Body Slams' and the phrase 'Use Explosive Cask'). Unlike the Riven-facing pages the mirror complained about, the Executioner's Calling line on THIS entry is correct — Happy Hour is real healing and Grievous Wounds genuinely applies, so I left report[8].t and breakdown.late alone. Full-layer prose in this brief carries mojibake em dashes, so I edited only clean full-layer strings plus enum fields; the 'mid' paragraph still says 'his Cask has a longer cooldown than your R', which is true at R ranks 2-3 (100/85/70 vs 120/90/60) but FALSE at rank 1 where Riven's R is the longer of the two — worth a byte-exact fix.
